places.name: Cerro Alegre & Cerro Concepción
places.ai_summary: Cerro Alegre and Cerro Concepción are vibrant neighborhoods known for their colorful houses, street art, and bohemian vibe.

opening_hours.notes: Best explored on foot during daylight.

places.place_tip: Bring a camera to capture the stunning murals and views.

places.name: La Sebastiana (Pablo Neruda’s House)
places.ai_summary: La Sebastiana is the former home of Pablo Neruda, now a museum showcasing his life and eclectic collections.

opening_hours.notes: Last entry is 30 minutes before closing.

places.place_tip: Book tickets in advance to avoid queues.

places.ai_summary: The Ascensor Artillería Funicular is a historic elevator offering panoramic views of Valparaíso’s port and hills.

opening_hours.notes: Check for maintenance schedules before visiting.

places.place_tip: Take the funicular at sunset for the best views.

places.name: Valparaíso Street Art Walls
places.ai_summary: The Valparaíso Street Art Walls are an open-air gallery showcasing impressive murals and street art by local and international artists.

opening_hours.notes: Best viewed during the day for photography.

places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes for walking tours.

places.name: Museo a Cielo Abierto
places.ai_summary: Museo a Cielo Abierto is an open-air museum in Valparaíso, featuring a collection of murals and sculptures by renowned artists.

opening_hours.notes: Visit during the day for the best experience.

places.place_tip: Combine with a visit to Cerro Alegre for a full day of art and culture.

places.name: Plaza Sotomayor
places.ai_summary: Plaza Sotomayor is a historic square in Valparaíso, surrounded by impressive monuments and buildings, and a popular spot for tourists and locals alike.

opening_hours.notes: A great place to start a walking tour of the city.

places.place_tip: Check out the naval monument and the surrounding architecture.

attribution.title: Catedral de Valparaíso
attribution.author: Robert Cutts from Bristol, England, UK
attribution.description:
This photo and those that follow were taken during our second visit to Valparaiso on 30 September. 

Valparaiso Cathedral is dedicated to the Virgen of Carmen and is the mother church of the Diocese of Valparaiso. It was built between 1930 and 1950 in the Gothic style on land donated by Joan Ross Edwards. It was restored after the earthquake of 1971 and 1985 .

places.name: Muelle Prat Port Walk
places.ai_summary: The Muelle Prat Port Walk is a scenic promenade along Valparaíso’s waterfront, offering views of the port, hills, and colorful buildings.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the evening for sunset views.

places.place_tip: Enjoy fresh seafood at the nearby restaurants.

places.name: Palacio Baburizza Art Museum
places.ai_summary: The Palacio Baburizza Art Museum is an art museum in Valparaíso, housed in a beautiful historic palace with a collection of Chilean and European art.

opening_hours.notes: Last entry is 30 minutes before closing.

places.place_tip: Check out the stunning views from the palace gardens.

places.name: Reina Victoria Funicular
places.ai_summary: The Reina Victoria Funicular is a historic funicular railway in Valparaíso, offering scenic views of the city and the bay.

opening_hours.notes: Check for maintenance schedules before visiting.

places.place_tip: Take the funicular at sunset for a romantic view.

places.name: Cerro Bellavista
places.ai_summary: Cerro Bellavista is a hill in Valparaíso, known for its artistic community, colorful houses, and panoramic views of the city.

opening_hours.notes: Best explored on foot. Be cautious at night.

places.place_tip: Visit the Pablo Neruda’s house and the open-air museum.

places.place_tip: Start early to avoid crowds and heat.
